subject: RFI: Operator credentials and evidence for isolated deployment

Cc: ops@kitecloud.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Operator credentialing and evidence for isolated deployment

Sergio —

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, Hale Therapeutics is validating vendor operator practices for air‑gapped/on‑prem deployments. Please find attached our operator questionnaire (hale_operator_questionnaire.xlsx). Our security and procurement teams are especially looking for the following pieces of evidence: 

- Operator account lifecycle (creation, revocation) examples
- Operator role matrix and separation of duties
- Training completion logs and runbook excerpts for emergency operator procedures
- Mechanism for operator credential transport/rotation in isolated environments

Can Redwood provide evidentiary artifacts (redacted where necessary) and a brief timeline for delivery? We need to present items to procurement by Aug 6.

Best,
David
David Ortez
Director, Vendor Security & Procurement
Hale Therapeutics
Attachment: hale_operator_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78 KB)

Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Operator credentialing and evidence for isolated deployment

David —

Appreciate the questionnaire; we received the XLSX and have started a pass. High level answers below and we'll attach artifacts in the next message: 

- Operator lifecycle: we maintain an auditable operator lifecycle via our internal IAM + RBAC service. We will provide an anonymized export showing a recent onboarding and a forced-revocation event.
- Roles & SoD: Redwood defines three operator tiers for Private deployments (Operator, Senior Operator, Site Admin). We'll provide the role matrix and mapping to actions (start/stop nodes, rotate keys, emergency rollback).
- Training & runbooks: we have a certified operator training curriculum and a set of MOPs; we can share runbook excerpts and training completion logs (redacted). Priyom will pull the logs.
- Credential transport: for isolated installs we use an ephemeral credential handoff process (airlock transfer + signed manifest) and optional hardware keywrap with customer KMS. We will include the diagram and a short writeup.

Target timeline: we can deliver a curated evidence bundle by Tue, Aug 3, and a recorded walkthrough + Q&A the week of Aug 9 if that works for you. 

Action items: Vanessa to compile runbooks & proof; Priyom to export training logs; I'll prepare a short narrative on credential handoff.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference
Sergio.Alvarez@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_operator_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, stub)

Subject: Re: RFI: Operator credentialing and evidence for isolated deployment

Sergio —

Thanks — timeline looks good. A couple of clarifying asks from Security:

1) For the operator lifecycle extract, can you include timestamps for provisioning and deprovisioning events (UTC)? We need to show evidence of prompt removal after termination.
2) For credential handoff, what controls ensure the manifest cannot be replayed by a compromised operator? Is there an HSM-backed secret wrap, or a short-lived certificate exchange?
3) Training logs: we only need the last 12 months of completions. CSV is fine; please redact email addresses but keep unique operator ids.

If you can confirm those three items in the evidence bundle, procurement will accept the package. Also confirm if the walkthrough can be recorded and whether recordings are retained.

Appreciate the quick turn.
David
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: David Ortez <david.ortez@hale-thera.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Operator credentialing and evidence for isolated deployment

Hi David — forwarding the bundle below and answering your three clarifications inline. Replying on behalf of the evidence team.

--- Answer: Provisioning/deprovisioning timestamps ---
We attached operator-training-logs.csv with columns: operator_id, completion_timestamp_utc, course_id, status. The lifecycle export (included in the S3 link) contains audit events with UTC timestamps for create/disable/revoke actions (example rows are redacted but preserved timestamps). We will not include PII; operator_id is an internal opaque id.

--- Answer: Manifest replay protections ---
Our handshake for airlocked credential handoff uses a nonce + signed manifest pattern. The manifest is signed by the operator runner (private key stored in an HSM on the deployer appliance) and includes a one-time nonce, expiry window, and hash of the wrapped secret. The receiving host confirms nonce freshness and validates signature via the public key that the customer injects at install time. We document the flow and include sequence diagrams in mops_summary.pdf. Where customers require hardware wrapping, we support vendor HSM keywrap flows (explicitly supported in our on‑prem installer).

--- Answer: Training logs retention/format ---
The CSV covers rolling 12 months; we removed emails and replaced them with operator_id. We can provide additional metadata (course version, cert id) if helpful.

Attachments included in the bundle:
- operator-training-logs.csv (CSV, 42 KB)
- mops_summary.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)
- lifecycle_events_sample.csv (CSV, 16 KB)

Next steps: Monica Patel from our services team will schedule a short remote walkthrough (20–30 minutes) to step through the manifest flow and show a redacted lifecycle export. Monica — can you propose two slots next week?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Product Security Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: operator-training-logs.csv; mops_summary.pdf; lifecycle_events_sample.csv
